# Part 2: Postprocessing/Visualization of a pore-network model

After compiling and running the code, the invasion/trapping state and the pore-body
capillary pressure/saturation can be visualized with the open source visualization
application ParaView.

Load your results into ParaView, either via `File` -> `Open` -> select `pcsaturation_pnm.pvd` (or a single `pcsaturation_pnm-*.vtp` step), or directly from the terminal:
```bash
paraview build-cmake/examples/porenetwork_pcsaturation/pcsaturation_pnm.pvd &
```

For general instructions on how to represent pore bodies as spheres/boxes and pore throats as lines/tubes (with radii scaled by `poreInscribedRadius`/`throatInscribedRadius`), see [Part 4 of the pore-network upscaling example](../../porenetwork_upscaling/doc/postprocessing.md) -- the same technique applies here; only the fields of interest differ, as described below.

## Fields specific to this example

This example additionally writes the following per-timestep fields, which are the ones most relevant for inspecting drainage/imbibition/trapping:

* **`invaded`** (cell data, per throat) -- `1` if the throat currently carries non-wetting phase, `0` otherwise.
* **`trapped`** (cell data, per throat) -- `1` if the throat is invaded but has lost its connected path back to the inlet (i.e. is part of a non-wetting-phase cluster whose local capillary pressure is frozen). Only ever `1` where `invaded` is also `1`.
* **`pc`** / **`sw`** (point data, per pore) -- the local capillary pressure and wetting-phase saturation of each pore body.
* **`pcEntry`** / **`pcSnapOff`** (cell data, per throat) -- the precomputed entry and snap-off threshold capillary pressures.

A useful way to see trapping directly in ParaView: color the throats (e.g. as tubes, see the linked instructions above) by `trapped`, and step through the time series with the animation controls -- invaded-but-trapped clusters (value `1`) appear as isolated red pockets once the imbibition leg starts retreating, exactly as in Fig. 3 of the [main description](../README.md).
